'''Davender Singh Malik''' (14 August 1958 – 13 May 2025) was an Indian-American mathematician and professor of mathematics and [[computer science]] at [[Creighton University]].

==Education==
Malik attended the [[University of Delhi]] in New Delhi, India, receiving his bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics, where he won the Prof. Ram Behari Gold Medal in 1980 for his high marks.<ref name=indiawest>{{cite news | title=Davender Malik Named for New Chair in Creighton Mathematics | work=India-West | date=24 November 2013 | url=http://www.indiawest.com/news/global_indian/davender-malik-named-for-new-chair-in-creighton-mathematics/article_f2f3434e-e461-5546-9b46-9b0b017872a3.html?mode=jqm | accessdate=29 July 2018 | archive-date=30 July 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730050445/http://www.indiawest.com/news/global_indian/davender-malik-named-for-new-chair-in-creighton-mathematics/article_f2f3434e-e461-5546-9b46-9b0b017872a3.html?mode=jqm | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | author=Fulvia Furinghetti | title=The First Century of the International Commission on Mathematical Instruction (1908-2008): Ram Behari | work=[[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction|ICMI]] | publisher=Department of Mathematics, University of Genova | url=http://www.icmihistory.unito.it/portrait/behari.php | accessdate=2015-06-24}}</ref> Then at the [[University of Waterloo]] in Ontario, Canada, he received a master's degree in [[pure mathematics]].<ref name=indiawest/> In the United States, Malik went to [[Ohio University]], earning an M.S. in [[computer science]], and a Ph.D. in mathematics in 1985, writing his dissertation on "A Study of Q-Hypercyclic Rings."<ref name=indiawest/><ref>{{cite web | title=A study of q-hypercyclic rings | work=ALICE Catalog | publisher=Ohio University Libraries | url=http://alice.library.ohiou.edu/record=b1485010~S7 | accessdate=2015-06-23 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Career==
In 1985, Malik joined the faculty of [[Creighton University]], teaching in the mathematics department. In 2013, he became the first holder of the Frederick H. and Anna K. Scheerer Endowed Chair in Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web | author=Scott Prewitt | title=Malik awarded endowed chair of mathematics department | date=30 October 2013 | work=Creightonian | url=http://www.creightonian.com/news/article_582c5022-4183-11e3-a871-0019bb30f31a.html | accessdate=2015-06-24}}</ref>  His research focused on [[ring theory]], [[abstract algebra]], [[information science]], and [[fuzzy mathematics]], including fuzzy [[automata theory]], [[fuzzy logic]], and applications of [[fuzzy set theory]] in other disciplines.<ref name=indiawest/><ref name=sketch>{{cite web | title=Dr. Davender Malik: Biographical Sketch and Research Interests | date=30 August 2013 | work=Student Research Opportunities, Department of Mathematics | publisher=College of Arts and Sciences, Creighton University | url=http://math.creighton.edu/Student/Research/index.htm | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070818181039/http://math.creighton.edu/Student/Research/index.htm | url-status=dead | archive-date=18 August 2007 | accessdate=2015-06-24 }}</ref>

In the academic community, Malik was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and [[Phi Kappa Phi]].<ref name=chair>{{cite web|title=Planned Giving |work=Creighton Giving |publisher=[[Creighton University]] |url=http://www.creighton.edu/giving/news/plannedgiving/ |accessdate=2015-06-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304194029/http://www.creighton.edu/giving/news/plannedgiving/ |archivedate=2016-03-04 }}</ref>  Within his community, he co-created a Creighton program in which faculty help area high school students pursue scientific research, to be published in their own student journal.<ref>{{cite web|title=High school research program inspires young scholars |work=News Center |publisher=Creighton University |date=5 December 2014 |url=http://www.creighton.edu/publicrelations/newscenter/news/2014/december2014/december52014/hsresearchnr120514/ |accessdate=2015-06-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328223819/http://www.creighton.edu/publicrelations/newscenter/news/2014/december2014/december52014/hsresearchnr120514/ |archivedate=2015-03-28 }}</ref>

Malik published more than 45 papers and 18 books.<ref name=named>{{cite web|title=Malik to be Named for New Chair in Creighton Mathematics |date=3 September 2013 |work=News Center |publisher=[[Creighton University]] |url=http://www.creighton.edu/publicrelations/newscenter/news/2013/september2013/september32013/malikscheerenr090313/ |accessdate=2015-06-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907210431/http://www.creighton.edu/publicrelations/newscenter/news/2013/september2013/september32013/malikscheerenr090313/ |archivedate=2015-09-07 }}</ref> He created a computer science line of textbooks that includes extensive and complete programming examples, exercises, and case studies throughout using [[programming languages]] such as [[C++]] and [[Java (programming language)|Java]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.course.com/programming/malik.cfm |title=Course Technology - Programming}}</ref>

==Death==
Malik died on 13 May 2025, at the age of 66.<ref>[https://heafeyheafey.com/davender-s-malik-ph-d/ Davender Singh Malik, Ph.D.]</ref>

==Books==
The books he wrote include:
;Programming
* ''C++ Programming: From Problem Analysis to Program Design'' (1st ed., 2002; 8th ed. 2017)
* ''C++ Programming: Program Design Including Data Structures'' (1st ed., 2002; 8th ed. 2017)
* ''Data Structures Using C++'' (1st ed., 2003; 2nd ed. 2010)
* ''Data Structures Using Java'' (2003)
* ''Java programming: From Problem Analysis to Program Design'' (1st ed., 2003; 5th ed. 2012)
* ''Java programming: Program Design including Data structures'' (2006)
* ''Java programming: Guided Learning With Early Objects'' (2009)
* ''Introduction to C++ Programming, Brief Edition'' (2009)
;Mathematics
* ''Fundamentals of Abstract Algebra'' (1997)
* ''Fuzzy Commutative Algebra'' (1998)
* ''Fuzzy Discrete Structures'' (2000)
* ''Fuzzy Mathematics in Medicine'' (2000)
* ''Fuzzy Automata and Languages: Theory and Applications'' (2002)
* ''Fuzzy Semigroups'' (2003)
* ''Application of Fuzzy Logic to Social Choice Theory'' (2015)
